definitions: To seem promising or effective in theory, but not necessarily in practice.
To appear to be a good idea or plan when written down or discussed, but may not work out well in reality.
examples: The new business plan looks good on paper, but we need to see if it's feasible.
Her resume looked good on paper, but her interview performance was disappointing.
The proposal for the new project looks good on paper, but the implementation will be challenging.
